tenet: Use state machines / typestate — encode a multi-state protocol so illegal operations don't compile
why_discriminating: A three-state protocol (closed -> listening -> established) is harder to fully type-encode than a two-state builder. The naive solution is one structure holding a state value where every operation is always callable; the skillful solution indexes `Conn` by its state so `send` only accepts an established connection and `Conn.closed.send "hello"` fails elaboration. This is the 'hard' task expected to leave headroom for a body-optimizer.
prompt: Model a network connection in Lean 4. A connection starts closed; a closed connection can be told to `listen`; a listening connection can `accept` to become established; an established connection can `send` data. Provide `Conn.closed` returning a fresh closed connection, plus the operations `listen`, `accept`, and `send` (taking a `String`) — each usable with dot notation (e.g. `c.listen`). Output only top-level declarations — no `main`, no `#check`/`#eval` demos.
